topic: Index admission cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease

audits.title: 225 The Management of Acute Cholecystitis in a District General setting: An Audit of Practice
audits.standard: NICE: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis of acute cholecystitis
audits.setting: Salisbury District Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: 285 (87%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days; of 43 who did not, 31 had clinically justified delay; 285/297 (96%) met the NICE standard.

cycle2.result: Re-audit showed significant improvement (no figures reported).

audits.other_findings: Poor documentation was the most common cause of failure; other reasons were awaiting ERCP/MRCP, unfit for surgery and patient choice.
audits.citation: Robinson P, Jones S, Metcalf A, Bond A. 225 The Management of Acute Cholecystitis in a District General setting: An Audit of Practice. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.020.

audits.title: 267 An Audit of The Management of Acute Cholecystitis At ELHT
audits.standard: NICE CG188: offer early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis for acute cholecystitis

cycle1.result: 51 (47%) had laparoscopic cholecystectomy within a week of diagnosis.

audits.other_findings: Modifiable reasons were lack of theatre capacity and consultant decisions to delay; a dedicated hot gallbladder list was recommended.
audits.citation: Ahmed A. 267 An Audit of The Management of Acute Cholecystitis At ELHT. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.029.

audits.title: 963 Management of Acute Gallstone-Related Complications at Great Western Hospital (GWH): Re-Audit
audits.standard: Current guidelines on cholecystectomy within target time frame after diagnosis; national average 15% (RCSEng)
audits.setting: Surgical department, Great Western Hospital, Swindon

cycle1.result: Very low number of patients had cholecystectomy within the target time frame; biliary readmissions 58%

cycle2.result: 10.7% increase in timely cholecystectomies, overall compliance 14%; biliary readmissions 37%

audits.other_findings: 47.3% of patients were still awaiting surgery, but the waiting list fell by 5.2% in 1 year despite COVID-19.
audits.citation: Castelhano R, Bartlett J, Wooler H, Theofilis A, Mahmoud A, Shamali A. 963 Management of Acute Gallstone-Related Complications at Great Western Hospital (GWH): Re-Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.761.

audits.title: EP.TH.917An Audit of Compliance with NICE guidelines for Acute Cholecystitis
audits.standard: NICE and RCS: laparoscopic cholecystectomy during same admission or within 7 days
audits.setting: Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Only 10% had cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis.

audits.other_findings: 14% of those discharged without surgery were readmitted with gallstone complications; mean time to surgery after discharge 125.8 days; a hot gallbladder pathway is proposed.

audits.title: P-EGS07 Two years of Acute Biliary Admissions at a tertiary care centre over the Covid-19 pandemic: a closed loop audit with implementation of an acute referral system
audits.standard: AUGIS: laparoscopic cholecystectomy on index admission for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis, ideally within 72 hours
audits.setting: Central London tertiary care centre (Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital)

cycle1.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 98.2 weeks.

audits.intervention: Dedicated e-referral system for patients who did not have cholecystectomy on index admission.

cycle2.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 47.7 weeks.

audits.other_findings: Readmissions fell by 23.3% in choledocholithiasis, 17.4% biliary colic, 16.7% ascending cholangitis, 12.8% acute cholecystitis and 8.3% gallstone pancreatitis. 243 patients in total across both years.
audits.citation: Refalo A, White A, Widlund H, Ebied H. P-EGS07 Two years of Acute Biliary Admissions at a tertiary care centre over the Covid-19 pandemic: a closed loop audit with implementation of an acute referral system. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.

audits.title: P-EGS14 From Gallstone Disease to Cholecystectomy: An audit looking at the waiting times for cholecystectomy in a small District General Hospital
audits.standard: AUGIS guidelines: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours (biliary colic, cholecystitis), 2 weeks (gallstone pancreatitis) or 6 weeks
audits.setting: Emergency general surgery, Southport and Ormskirk Hospital (district general hospital)

cycle1.result: Biliary colic (9 pre-COVID, 5 during COVID): none had LC within 72 hours. Cholecystitis (20 pre-COVID, 16 during COVID): none within 72 hours. Gallstone pancreatitis: only 1 patient had LC within 2 weeks.

audits.other_findings: Waiting times were longer during COVID. Delays linked to limited ultrasound, staff and theatre access; a hot gallbladder service with dedicated theatre slots was proposed.
audits.citation: Mewse J, Ledda V, Connor E, Mason P. P-EGS14 From Gallstone Disease to Cholecystectomy: An audit looking at the waiting times for cholecystectomy in a small District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab430.074.

audits.title: P17 Acute cholecystectomy service quality improvement
audits.standard: More than 80% of eligible patients to undergo cholecystectomy within 8 days of acute biliary presentation

cycle1.result: HES showed 20% compliance; 60% incorrectly coded; of correctly coded, 58% had cholecystectomy within 8 days; 70% of weekend biliary ultrasound requests not performed.

audits.intervention: Stakeholder consultation and a pathway disseminated via education, trust induction and a protocol, with increased ultrasound provision (4 weekday and 2 weekend patients/day), one theatre session per week and senior clinician-led coding.

cycle2.result: 100% of eligible patients had cholecystectomy within 8 days; no waiting list patient had an emergency admission.

audits.other_findings: 21% of waiting list patients had previous biliary attendances and 39% were not referred for surgery.
audits.citation: Hammer C, O'Brien J, Pencavel T. P17 Acute cholecystectomy service quality improvement. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac231.017.

audits.title: EGS P22 Management of acute cholecystitis during the Covid-19 pandemic - A complete cycle
audits.standard: NICE guidelines: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 1 week of diagnosis
audits.setting: Warrington and Halton Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Admission covid swabs 64.7%, interval covid swabs 0%; hot gallbladder rate 8.8%; median admission to operation 4 days; readmission for complications 20.6%.

audits.intervention: Green elective surgical pathway, clinical priority coding for elective surgery, a hot gallbladder pathway, and a dedicated weekend and evening list; findings presented at departmental meeting.

cycle2.result: Admission covid swabs 97.3%, interval covid swabs 54.1%; hot gallbladder rate 10.8%; median admission to operation 1.5 days; readmission for complications 29.7%.

audits.other_findings: Overall performance still behind NICE recommendation; theatre pressure and cancer fast-track priority during Covid-19 were identified as factors.
audits.citation: Islam M, Tan J, Oldfield F, English L, Tandon A, Al-Rashedy M. EGS P22 Management of acute cholecystitis during the Covid-19 pandemic - A complete cycle. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_9). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac404.087.

audits.title: ThTP1.11 Closed Loop Audit on The Timing of Hot Gallbladder Surgery
audits.standard: AUGIS 2016 and NICE 2021: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days of admission for hot gallbladder

cycle1.result: 75.3% had LC within 7 days; 24.7% within 3 days.

audits.intervention: Departmental teaching session and guideline posters.

cycle2.result: 68% had LC within 7 days; 36% within 3 days; average admission to LC 6.4 days.

audits.other_findings: Commonest causes of delay were waiting for ERCP/MRCP and theatre availability.
audits.citation: Shabana A, Patel M, Samra B, Pustula M, Zhuang Q. ThTP1.11 Closed Loop Audit on The Timing of Hot Gallbladder Surgery. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad241.250.

audits.title: 1162 Management of Acute Gallstone Disease at an Urban Acute Trust During the Pandemic – Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: National guidelines on early laparoscopic cholecystectomy for acute gallstone disease
audits.setting: Urban acute trust, Barking, Havering & Redbridge NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 49 patients had LC, only 20% performed acutely; 70% of acute operations were during re-admissions.

audits.intervention: Hot cholecystectomy list opened to other surgeons and acute LC encouraged on the emergency theatre list.

cycle2.result: 21% underwent LC, of which 52% were acute operations; 50% of emergency operations were in re-admissions.

audits.other_findings: Average wait from admission to LC in the initial cohort was 118.5 days; provision still does not comply with national guidelines.
audits.citation: Sharif M, Osilli D, Mukherjee D, Buhain R. 1162 Management of Acute Gallstone Disease at an Urban Acute Trust During the Pandemic – Closed-Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.187.

audits.title: 458 Post-COVID-19 Regularisation of Emergency Laparoscopic Cholecystectomies: A Single-Centred Multi-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: AUGIS advice: emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 72 hours of diagnosing acute cholecystitis

cycle1.result: Median admission to theatre 106.5 hours; median length of stay 7.5 days.

cycle2.result: Median admission to theatre 70.7 hours (IQR 48.4-107.7); median admission to imaging 11 hours; median length of stay 5.6 days.

audits.other_findings: 2021 cycle: admission to theatre 76.7 hours, stay 5.3 days. 2022: 9.2% subtotal cholecystectomies, 14.8% post-op complications including 2.2% bile leaks.

audits.standard: NICE and AUGIS guidelines (laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days)

cycle1.result: Only 18.4% underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy, median time to surgery 95 days (IQR 43.5–324.5) versus recommended 7 days; median delay 5 days for MRCP and 8 days for ERCP; median LOS 8 days; 49.6% readmitted.

audits.title: 48 Audit on the Management of Patients Admitted with Acute Gallstone Disease
audits.standard: Chole-QuIC target: 80% of eligible patients to have cholecystectomy within 8 days
audits.setting: East Surrey Hospital, district general hospital

cycle1.result: 31/53 (58.5%) eligible acute gallstone disease patients had cholecystectomy within 8 days; 25/40 fit acute cholecystitis patients had inpatient cholecystectomy.

audits.other_findings: 5/15 discharged acute cholecystitis patients were readmitted within 30 days; inpatient surgery had shorter wait (3 v 31 days) but longer fasting and stay.

audits.title: 29 Evaluating Adherence to NICE Guidelines for Urgent Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Acute Cholecystitis: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE: laparoscopic cholecystectomy within 7 days of acute cholecystitis diagnosis; Chole-QuIC benchmarks (top sites 20–60% within 8 days)
audits.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 18.2% (12/66) had surgery within 7 days. Only 5 cases used the hot gallbladder pathway, 40% (2/5) meeting the 7-day target. Average time to surgery 68 days.

audits.other_findings: Delays were due to waiting lists, booking issues, delayed presentation and comorbidity; optimising the hot gallbladder pathway recommended.
audits.citation: Ayyad M, Dhanjal R, Rehman Z, Sahloul M. 29 Evaluating Adherence to NICE Guidelines for Urgent Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy in Acute Cholecystitis: A Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_17). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf270.227.

audits.standard: Guideline-recommended cholecystectomy within 10 days for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis
audits.setting: District general hospital (Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: Of 73 patients fit for surgery, only 11% underwent cholecystectomy within 10 days.

audits.title: EP 368 Evaluating Missed Opportunities for Emergency Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Retrospective Single-Centre Audit
audits.setting: Department of General Surgery, Homerton University Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Only 3 patients had surgery within P2 targets; 79 (41%) had multiple booking requests; 52 (27%) potentially suitable for earlier emergency cholecystectomy, with deferral reasons documented for 8.

audits.other_findings: 89 (47%) proceeded directly to surgery after booking; contributing factors included waiting times, emergency theatre capacity, ERCP timing and loss to follow-up.
audits.citation: Nguyen D, Ramzi J, Hussein H, Aguilo R. EP 368 Evaluating Missed Opportunities for Emergency Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy: A Retrospective Single-Centre Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.578.
